label: September 21–27
title: “A Marvellous Work and a Wonder” —  Isaiah 13–14; 22; 24

items.text: Prophets are called to warn about the consequences of sin. Isaiah, fearless in his task, delivered bold warnings to mighty kingdoms, including Israel and Judah. Yet, amidst prophesied destructions, Isaiah also foresaw a message of hope, restoration, and renewal through the Lord’s invitation to return.

Isaiah’s message to Babylon, symbolizing pride, greed, and sin, remains relevant today. By examining the pride of the Babylonian king and comparing it to Satan’s pride, we find warnings for ourselves. The Savior offers rest from our sorrow and fear, inviting us to rely on His redeeming power.

The Savior’s mission, encompassing His atoning sacrifice, Resurrection, and Second Coming, is a core teaching of Isaiah. As we study these passages, we are reminded of His power to overcome death and bring victory. Let us bear testimony of Jesus Christ and rely on His teachings and perfect love.

Turning away from the Lord brings spiritual danger. Isaiah warned that straying from Him leads to consequences likened to a sad, empty earth, drunkenness, hunger, and thirst. These attitudes and actions are spiritually perilous, emphasizing the importance of staying close to the Lord always.

Isaiah 29:14 describes a “marvellous work and a wonder” that the Lord would perform. Although no one alive at Isaiah’s time saw it, we are living in it today. We are not merely observers but active participants in this divine restoration and renewal of His promised blessings.

The Lord can restore what is lost or broken. When we turn away from Him, Satan tempts us to believe return or healing is impossible. However, Isaiah’s prophecies reveal the marvelous ways the Lord helps us return, offering hope and renewal through His divine power.

“He will swallow up death in victory” (Isaiah 25:8). This profound promise points to the Savior’s ultimate triumph over death through His Atonement and Resurrection. It assures us that through Him, we can overcome all adversies and find eternal life.

The Lord will make “the parched ground … become a pool, and the thirsty land springs of water” (Isaiah 35:7). This imagery represents the spiritual refreshment and abundant blessings that come from returning to the Lord. His power transforms barrenness into life and hope.

Pride, greed, and sin are symbolized by ancient Babylon, but they also surround us today. By recognizing these patterns, we can heed Isaiah’s warnings and seek the Savior’s rest from sorrow and fear, finding solace and strength in His everlasting love and power.

Isaiah’s prophecies remind us that turning away from the Lord leads to spiritual emptiness. The Lord, in His mercy, sends prophets to warn us and offers pathways back to Him. Staying close to the Lord is essential for our spiritual well-being and eternal safety.
